prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the steep vertical geometry of an unfinished masonry shaft, rendering the foreground jagged brick ledges and columns bright white-grey (~0.3–1.5 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach) and the receding plastered side walls as smooth gradients fading into black at the shaft floor (~3–4 m below). Across frames 1 to 5, as the wearer moves rightward and leans over the opening, the brick column shifts from the centre-right (~0.8–1.2 m) to the extreme right edge (~0.3–0.5 m) while the stepped brick wall on the left moves into the immediate lower-left foreground (~0.3–0.8 m), exposing the deep central drop between them. Compared to the dimly lit RGB strip, the depth map makes it much easier to read the continuous 3D slant of the side walls, the stepped depth of individual protruding bricks, and the recessed depth of the horizontal white pipe (~2.5 m down) spanning the shaft above the lower person. However, the map is unreliable for small foreground objects and dark recesses: the trowel and level resting on the ledge within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m) are smoothed into the ledge surface, and the person standing ~3–4 m below (facing and looking upward toward the wearer) is swallowed by the black background in frames 1–4 before appearing only as a faint grey blob in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: In frame 3, the segmentation map isolates a brown 'person' mask for the worker standing ~3–4 m below at the bottom of the shaft between the side walls, who is facing and looking upward toward the camera wearer while holding a small object within their own arm's reach. Aside from that single detection, the map fails to track the worker in frames 1–2 (where they are in shadow and partly occluded by the foreground ledge) and frames 4–5 (where they shift slightly left relative to the frame as the wearer peers deeper over the edge). While the frame 3 mask helps separate the distant worker's silhouette from the dark shaft background where RGB contrast is low, the segmentation map is overwhelmingly unreliable across the sequence. It completely misses the trowel and level within the wearer's arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m on the lower ledge) and hallucinates false labels onto the surrounding masonry: misclassifying the walls and brick pillar in frame 1 as gigantic 'person' and 'tie' masks, the left-side stepped bricks (~0.8–1.2 m) and right brick pillar (~0.5–1.0 m) in frame 2 as 'carrot' and 'person', the right-edge bricks (~0.4 m) in frame 3 as 'person', and the bottom-left bricks (~0.4 m) in frame 4 as 'teddy bear'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. From the RGB strip, the camera wearer's hands and body remain out of the field of view behind the camera (with a trowel and level resting within arm's reach at ~0.5–0.8 m on the foreground ledge in frames 1–3), while another person stands ~3–4 m below at the base of the narrow shaft, ~1–1.5 m below the horizontal white pipe. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer shifts rightward and tilts downward over the gap between the left and right brick walls, this lower person passes from partial occlusion behind the foreground ledge in frames 1–2 into clear overhead view in frames 3–5, facing and looking up toward the wearer with their arms angled forward holding an item within their reach. Because the pose estimator outputs nothing at all, it adds no spatial clarity over the RGB frames and is completely unreliable under this steep top-down viewing angle, ~3–4 m distance, and dim shaft lighting.
